paper_title: MICROSCOPE mission: first constraints on the violation of the weak equivalence principle by a light scalar dilaton
coupling_convention: Yukawa strength alpha relative to gravity (dimensionless), for scalar coupled to baryon number B
notes: MICROSCOPE first WEP results (Eotvos parameter eta = (-1 +/- 27)e-15 at 2-sigma) used to constrain a scalar fifth force. Primary text-quoted bounds: |alpha| < 1e-11 for coupling to baryon number B, and |alpha| < 1e-12 for coupling to B-L, both valid for scalar masses below 1e-12 eV (range > few 1e5 m); bounds saturate (mass-independent) for m < 1e-14 eV down to massless, so encoded as a flat line over 1e-18 to 1e-12 eV. Chose ScalarBaryon (q=B result) per the WEP/Eotvos nature of the test; the paper also constrains B-L Yukawa (could map to VectorBL if mediator were a vector, but here it is a scalar), generic dilaton parameters (D_mtilde, D_e in figures only), and |d_e| < ~1e-4 for a photon-coupled dilaton (ScalarPhoton candidate: [[1e-18,1e-4],[1e-11,1e-4]]). Multiple coupling types discussed, hence confidence capped at 0.5. Not a dark-matter search; no DM density assumed.
